Hi Mira / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a couple clarifying questions so we can map the right deployment option: Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem.

Key points I heard:
- You need strong separation between CardioHealth data and any other tenant traffic (regulatory requirement).
- Control-plane visibility and key custody are important for auditability.
- Possible preference for 'customer-managed network' and HSM-backed keys if we go private.

Questions to help qualify the next step:
1) Do you require the Redwood control plane to be accessible only from within your VPC (i.e., private control plane) or is an internet-accessible control plane acceptable if all data egress is restricted?
2) Is BYOK/HSM mandatory for the initial pilot or negotiable post-PoC?
3) Any minimum uptime SLO expectations we should validate against our Dedicated offering?

Suggested next steps:
- If Private VPC is preferred: schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security and our private-deploy engineer (Ben).
- If Dedicated is acceptable: we can provide an ops playbook and SLA example for dedicated pools, plus a quick BOM for capacity planning.

Attachments: none on my side yet — I will share our architecture excerpt and SOC2 snippet in my follow-up (short PDFs).

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the recap — that captures our high-level needs. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Private control plane: preferred. Our security team prefers the control plane endpoints to be reachable only from within our VPC (or via a customer-managed transit/VPN). Public control plane with strict egress controls is a fallback but will require additional legal reviews.
2) BYOK/HSM: mandatory for production (we can be flexible for an initial PoC if the key custodian is our security team and we have clear rotations).
3) Uptime SLO: target is 99.9% for inference latency-sensitive endpoints (we understand there are tradeoffs if using private/on-prem hardware).

I attached our internal 'data security checklist' that outlines must-haves (networking, key custody, logging). Also adding Samir (infra) to help schedule the deep-dive.

Appreciate the clear answers. Quick responses inline below.

- Private control plane: understood — we can support a private control-plane deployment in our Redwood Private offering (control plane endpoints in your VPC with mutual TLS). We will need an initial network diagram from your side (VPC, subnets, transit/VPN) and a brief IP allowlist window to provision.
- BYOK/HSM: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM-backed envelopes. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed) we offer envelope encryption with Redwood KMS; BYOK is not available in the first Dedicated tier.
- Uptime SLO: our Dedicated product has a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for inference endpoints on reserved capacity; Private (VPC/on-prem) uptime depends on your infra and we provide runbooks + optional managed on-call.

I attached two short files: 'redwood-arch-overview.pdf' (private deployment topology sketch) and 'soc2-excerpt.pdf' (controls summary relevant to logging and audit).
